purpose: Milnacipran is used to help manage fibromyalgia, a condition that causes widespread pain and fatigue throughout the body. It helps reduce the pain and improve how you feel day to day. It is not used as an antidepressant in the US, but it works on brain chemicals that affect how your body senses pain.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers called serotonin and norepinephrine to help control pain signals. In fibromyalgia, those signals can get turned up too high, making everything feel more painful than it should. Milnacipran helps keep more of those chemicals available in your brain, which helps turn down the pain signals and makes you feel better.
common_side_effects: Nausea, headache, constipation, dizziness, hot flashes or sweating, dry mouth, increased heart rate or blood pressure, and trouble sleeping are the most common side effects. Nausea often improves after the first few weeks as your body adjusts.
warnings: This medication carries a warning about an increased risk of suicidal thoughts, especially in young adults under 25, so let your doctor know right away if you feel more depressed or have unusual thoughts. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms. Tell your doctor if you have high blood pressure, heart problems, liver or kidney disease, glaucoma, or if you take other medications, especially blood thinners or other antidepressants. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication.
typical_dosing: You usually start with a low dose of 12.5 mg once a day for the first day, then the dose is gradually increased over about one week up to the target dose of 50 mg twice a day. Your doctor may adjust this based on how you respond. Always take it exactly as prescribed and do not stop without your doctor's guidance.
